walkthroughs.body_html:
HL Regional Option: History of Europe — a core area of History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

HL Regional Option: History of Europe brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with HL Regional Option: History of Europe.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which Bolshevik slogan summarised Lenin's April Theses?
options: Peace, Land, Bread
Workers of the world unite
Liberte, egalite, fraternite
Better dead than red

mcqs.q: What was the immediate cause of the February Revolution?
options: German invasion
Bread shortages in Petrograd
Lenin's return from Switzerland
Kerensky's offensive

mcqs.q: Why was Jenner's smallpox vaccination significant in 1796?
options: Jenner used penicillin to cure smallpox.
He showed cowpox material could prevent smallpox safely — the first effective vaccine, though he did not know why it worked; germ theory came nearly a century later.
Jenner discovered germs and used them to make vaccines.
Luther's ideas spread because the Pope endorsed them.

mcqs.q: Why did Luther's 95 Theses spread so quickly in 1517?
options: Luther's ideas spread because the Pope endorsed them.
The printing press allowed rapid reproduction; existing critique of Church corruption and indulgence sales found ready audiences; German princes had political reasons to back Luther against Rome.
Luther's ideas spread because he was the first to criticise the Catholic Church.
The 1832 Reform Act allowed women to vote for the first time.
